sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is read without optional chaining, and mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty. WHY: any Google Meet booking where neither the organizer nor the event type has a destination calendar throws a TypeError, and booking creation fails. The old code used `?.`. HOW: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

WHAT: references for non-calendar results (video) now get `credentialId: undefined`, where they used to get result.credentialId. WHY: handleCancelBooking only deletes video meetings when the video reference has a credentialId, so Zoom/Daily meetings are no longer deleted on cancel. HOW: keep result.credentialId for every result type.

WHAT: the fallback only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, but it then searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, so it never matches a real calendar. WHY: the calendar id becomes undefined, which drops the old fallback to destinationCalendar.externalId and sends updates for legacy references to the wrong calendar or makes them fail. HOW: fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId.

WHAT: the deleteEvent fallback searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined. WHY: for references without externalCalendarId, the destination calendar fallback is lost and the delete falls back to the default calendar. If the event lives in a different calendar, it is left behind. HOW: use `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

WHAT: destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing. WHY: in collective events where the first host has no destination calendar, the other hosts' calendars are silently dropped, which is the case this PR is supposed to fix. HOW: default to `[]` instead of null.

WHAT: createEvent always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId. createAllCalendarEvents now calls it once per host credential, so every host's Office365 credential gets the first host's calendar id. WHY: a second collective host using Office365 posts to `/me/calendars/<host1-calendar-id>/events`, which does not exist in their account, so their event creation fails. HOW: pick the destination entry whose credentialId matches this credential, as GoogleCalendarService does.

WHAT: the recurring-series branch, which deletes the events of all updatedBookings for every user calendar credential, now sits inside the per-reference loop. WHY: with multiple calendar references, the same recurring events get one delete call per reference, which causes duplicate API calls and 404/410 errors. HOW: move the recurring deletion out of the reference loop so it runs once.

WHAT: the slug condition was flipped from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`. WHY: with billing enabled, the slug is set right away and also stored as requestedSlug, and with billing disabled, organizations are created with no slug. HOW: restore the negation.

WHAT: the catch block turns the plain Error thrown for an empty or invalid dynamicUserList into a generic 500 'Unable to load users'. WHY: a client input error comes back as a server error with its message hidden. HOW: throw `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })` directly for the validation failure.

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` comes from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it is `undefined` when there is no destination calendar. Callers now pass `[]` or `null` in that case. A Google Meet booking without a destination calendar then throws a TypeError on `.integration` instead of falling back to Cal Video.

The `find` fallback only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals that same falsy value. It therefore never returns the event's destination calendar, and the update goes out with an undefined calendarId instead of the destination calendar used before this PR.

When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, `destinationCalendar` is set to `null`. The following `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so collective team members' calendars are silently discarded. Initializing it to an empty array keeps them.

When there is no destination calendar, handleNewBooking now passes `destinationCalendar: null` and other callers pass `[]`. `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` then leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined, so reading `.integration` throws a TypeError. Every Google Meet booking without a destination calendar fails instead of falling back to Cal Video; using `?.integration` keeps the old fallback.

When evt.destinationCalendar is null or [] (handleNewBooking sets null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined. `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError for every Google Meet booking. This breaks booking creation in the very case the Cal Video fallback is meant to handle.

`destinationCalendar` is now an array, and when it is null or empty (handleNewBooking passes null if no event-type or organizer calendar is set), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. The old code read `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which handled null. The new code reads `.integration` on undefined, so every such booking throws a TypeError in EventManager.create. The fix is optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar`.

This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, but it searches `destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` using that same falsy value. The search never matches, so `selectedCalendar` is undefined. Before this change, the code fell back to the destination calendar's externalId.

The new catch block in loadUsers copies `error.message` from `PrismaClientKnownRequestError` into a 400 HttpError, which this public, unauthenticated booking endpoint sends back to the caller. Prisma error messages can include model, field and constraint names and query details, which exposes internal database structure. Log the Prisma error on the server and return a generic message to the client.

For COLLECTIVE events, every team member's full DestinationCalendar row (credentialId, externalId, userId) is now pushed into `evt.destinationCalendar`. `evt` is spread into the webhook payload, so other members' calendar IDs (often email addresses) and their credential IDs are sent to the webhook subscriber. Keep the team members' calendars off `evt`, for example by passing them to EventManager separately, or remove the field before building the payload.

The old code set `slug` only when team billing was disabled. The rewrite sets it only when billing is enabled, the same condition as `requestedSlug`. With billing enabled, orgs now get a final slug before payment or verification. With billing disabled, they get no slug at all.

The else branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, yet it looks for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`. That can never match a real calendar, so the destination calendar fallback is dead code and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined. The same expression appears in deleteEvent (lines 315-317). The fallback should pick the destination calendar that belongs to this credential, or the main host's calendar.

The old code used `result.credentialId` for non-calendar (video) results. The new ternary returns `undefined` for them, so video references are stored without the credential that created the meeting. Later updates and deletes of those meetings can no longer find the right credential.

`destinationCalendar` falls back to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one. In that case `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` does nothing, and the destination calendars of the other collective hosts are thrown away. Initializing to an empty array keeps those team calendars.

issues.descricao: Claims the optional chaining in mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant because a ternary already checks it.
issues.textoGolden: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

issues.descricao: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
issues.textoGolden: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId` against `null`/`undefined` and matches nothing (the same wrong pattern is duplicated in deleteEvent at lines 315-317).
WHY: When `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` are called without an externalCalendarId, `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` now resolves to `undefined` instead of the host's destination calendar externalId (old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), so the Google API is invoked with an undefined calendarId and the update/delete targets the wrong (or default) calendar or errors.
HOW: Find the destination calendar for the current credential (e.g. by credentialId) rather than comparing `externalId` to the already-falsy `externalCalendarId`, or restore the single fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

Dead computation in the fallback: the else branch runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet it calls `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, comparing every cal.externalId to undefined. Nothing can match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the fallback that previously returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is lost. Match the intended criterion (destination calendar's own externalId/credentialId), not the already-falsy externalCalendarId.

Same dead-computation defect in deleteEvent: the else branch executes only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet the predicate `(cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against undefined and can never match, so calendarId falls through to "primary" and the event is deleted from the wrong calendar instead of the booking's destination calendar. Fix the predicate to use the destination calendar's externalId (or credentialId) rather than the falsy externalCalendarId.

issues.descricao: The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.
issues.textoGolden: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

comentarios.texto: Organization creation no longer assigns a slug when team billing is disabled, while requestedSlug is also omitted in that mode. New self-hosted organizations therefore have neither publication field, and publish.handler rejects them because requestedSlug is missing. Restore the non-billing slug assignment.

WHAT: slug spread condition was inverted from ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && {slug}) to ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {slug} : {}). WHY: organizations get slug when billing enabled and lose it when disabled, opposite of prior contract and breaking slug/requestedSlug pairing. HOW: restore negation for slug branch.

issues.descricao: Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.
issues.textoGolden: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

comentarios.texto: Office365 creation always selects the first host's destination despite being invoked separately with each host's credential. A collective booking with distinct Office365 calendars sends the second host's token to the first host's calendar ID, causing failed or incorrectly targeted creation. Accept the credentialId supplied by CalendarManager and select the matching destination.

Select the destination belonging to the current credential rather than always taking the first array entry. EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination with that destination's credential, while passing the full event array each time. In a collective booking with two Outlook hosts, the second host therefore attempts to insert into the first host's calendar using the second host's token, typically failing instead of creating the second calendar event. Accept the credentialId passed by CalendarManager and match the destination by that ID (or pass a destination-specific event).

Select the destination belonging to the credential passed by CalendarManager, rather than always selecting the first array element. EventManager now invokes creation for each collective host with the full destination array. A second Office365 host therefore attempts to write to the first host's calendar using its own token, causing creation to fail or target the wrong calendar; meanwhile the saved reference records the second host's externalId.

issues.descricao: Claims updateAllCalendarEvents passes an undefined credential to updateEvent when reference.credentialId points to a credential that cannot be found.
issues.textoGolden: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

issues.descricao: The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining after destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`.
WHY: The previous code was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`, which was null-safe; now when `destinationCalendar` is null/empty (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets it to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one) and `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, destructuring yields `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`, crashing the booking creation flow.
HOW: Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` can be `undefined` because `evt.destinationCalendar` may now be null or an empty array (callers such as handleNewBooking pass `: null` / `: []`). The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, but the new line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` to preserve the null-safe fallback.

The Meet-location fallback destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When `destinationCalendar` is an empty array (which this PR now produces in many callers, e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts, the payment webhooks, confirm/editLocation/deleteCredential/requestReschedule handlers all set `[]` when there is no destination calendar), the destructured value is `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, aborting event creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` to preserve the previous optional-chained behavior.

issues.descricao: For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`.
WHY: For a COLLECTIVE event where neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, the evt field is set to `null` (lines 1063-1067), so the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` of the other hosts are dropped and those hosts are never invited — defeating the multi-host support this PR adds.
HOW: Initialize to an array (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing, or default the field to `[]` instead of `null`) so team destination calendars are always appended.

The optional push discards all collected team destinations when the organizer has no destination calendar. A collective booking with configured secondary hosts therefore creates none of their calendar events even though teamDestinationCalendars contains them. Initialize the array before appending the team destinations.

Initialize destinationCalendar to an array before appending collective hosts' destinations. When neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, it is set to null above, so optional push silently discards all the computed teamDestinationCalendars. Hosts with configured destination calendars consequently receive no calendar events.

issues.descricao: Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the previous non-calendar fallback `result.credentialId`.
WHY: For non-calendar results (video events) `referencesToCreate` now stores `credentialId: undefined` where it previously stored `result.credentialId`, so the persisted video reference loses its credentialId; later code that looks the reference up by credentialId (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts:491-502 deleting the video meeting, or EventManager.updateLocation) can no longer resolve the credential and the meeting is not cleaned up.
HOW: Keep the fallback for non-calendar results: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` (i.e. just `result.credentialId` for both branches).

The reference mapping discards credentialId for every video result. createMeeting returns the video credential ID, and handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its reference has that ID, so newly created video meetings are left behind on cancellation. Preserve result.credentialId for video results as well.

Retain result.credentialId for non-calendar references as well. The previous mapping saved the dedicated video integration's credential ID; this change unconditionally replaces it with undefined for video results, losing the association needed to identify the account that created the meeting during subsequent lifecycle operations.

issues.descricao: createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents fetch each missing host credential with a separate findUnique inside the loop instead of one batched query.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop performs a `prisma.credential.findUnique` on every destination whose credential is not found in the cached `this.calendarCredentials` (line 344); the same per-reference DB lookup was added in updateAllCalendarEvents at line 517.
WHY: For collective bookings with multiple hosts this turns one in-memory lookup into up to N sequential database round-trips added to the booking-creation hot path, scaling with host count.
HOW: Resolve all missing credential ids in a single batched query (`prisma.credential.findMany({ where: { id: { in: missingIds } } })`) before the loop and build a lookup map.

issues.descricao: updateLocation stores externalCalendarId and credentialId from updateEvent's result, which never returns them, so calendar references rewritten on location edit lose their calendar and credential and later updates or cancellations misroute.

comentarios.texto: updateLocation now reads externalId and credentialId exclusively from results, but CalendarManager.updateEvent returns neither field. Calendar references produced by location editing consequently lose their calendar and credential routing information, breaking subsequent updates or cancellation, particularly for secondary collective hosts. Return those fields from updateEvent or preserve them from the corresponding booking reference.

issues.descricao: Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

comentarios.texto: The new per-reference loop runs the recurring-series deletion branch for every host, but that branch still iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials and selects the first calendar reference in each occurrence. Canceling all remaining collective occurrences repeatedly deletes the owner's events while leaving secondary hosts' events untouched. For each occurrence, delete the reference matching the current host credential using the resolved calendarCredential.

For cancel-all-remaining recurring collective bookings, delete each updated booking's reference matching the current outer reference/credential. The new outer loop iterates all calendar references, but this inner block still iterates only the organizer's credentials and takes the first calendar reference of each booking. Every outer iteration therefore repeats deletion of the first host's event, while the additional hosts' recurring events remain on their calendars after cancellation.

issues.descricao: Google createEvent picks the target calendar only by matching credentialId, so destination calendars without a credentialId are ignored and events are created on the primary calendar instead.

comentarios.texto: createEvent now picks the target calendar only by matching credentialId. Destination calendars without a credentialId (handled by EventManager's integration-based branch) never match, so events are inserted into "primary" instead of the configured destination externalId as before.

issues.descricao: For destination calendars without a credentialId, createEvent is called without the externalId, so the booking reference is stored with an undefined externalCalendarId.

comentarios.texto: In the no-credentialId branch createEvent(c, event) is called without externalId, so EventResult.externalId is undefined. The booking reference's externalCalendarId, which used to come from evt.destinationCalendar.externalId, is now not stored, which breaks later update/delete targeting. Pass destination.externalId.

In the branch for destinations without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the externalId argument. CalendarManager.createEvent only returns `externalId` when it is passed in, and EventManager now stores `result.externalId` as externalCalendarId, so these booking references are saved with an undefined externalCalendarId. Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument, so the producer returns what the consumer stores.

issues.descricao: When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.
loadUsers forwards raw Prisma error messages to the client in a 400 response, exposing internal model and query details.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses `&&` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, and isTeamAdmin already matches ADMIN or OWNER roles, so the check passes only for OWNERs. WHY: Team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN, even though the variable name says admins should be allowed. HOW: Use `||`, or just call isTeamAdmin, which already covers owners.

WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails gets the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. WHY: An already-existing attendee who appears in the submitted list is treated as a new guest and gets a 'new booking scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests`.

WHAT: EventManager is built from the caller's (ctx.user) credentials, but updateCalendarAttendees updates the booking references that live in the organizer's calendar. WHY: When an attendee or team owner adds guests, the calendar update runs with credentials that don't own those events, so the organizer's calendar event never gets the new attendees, or the update throws. HOW: Build EventManager from booking.user and that user's credentials, as other booking handlers do.

WHAT: updateCalendarAttendees runs after attendees are already saved to the database, and it is not wrapped in error handling. WHY: If the calendar provider call fails, the client gets an error but the guests stay saved without emails, and a retry is rejected with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. HOW: Wrap the calendar update in try/catch and log the error so emails still go out and the mutation reports success.

WHAT: Blacklist entries are lowercased, but each guest email is compared with its original casing. WHY: Submitting a blacklisted address with any uppercase letter (e.g. `Bad@x.com`) gets past BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and the address is added and emailed. HOW: Lowercase the guest before comparing it to the blacklist and to existing attendees.

WHAT: The server schema accepts duplicate emails in `guests`, and the handler only removes guests that are already attendees, not repeats within the input. WHY: A direct API call with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows via createMany, because the uniqueness check exists only on the client. HOW: Add a refine that rejects duplicates (or dedupe with a Set in the handler).

WHAT: `guests` has no maximum length, and any booking attendee is allowed to call the mutation. WHY: An authenticated attendee can submit thousands of arbitrary addresses in one request, and each one gets a calendar-invite email sent in the organizer's name, which turns this endpoint into a spam relay. HOW: Cap the array size (e.g. `.max(10)`), on top of rate limiting.

The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71), but the incoming guest email is compared without normalisation, so `includes(guest)` misses any mixed-case version of a blacklisted address. An attacker can add a blacklisted guest by changing the case of a few letters (e.g. `Spam@Domain.com`). Lowercase the guest before the blacklist comparison.

sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts assumes `newGuests` lists only newly added attendees and sends them the full AttendeeScheduledEmail invite. The handler instead passes the raw `guests` input, which can include emails that were already attendees. Those existing attendees then get a fresh booking confirmation instead of the add-guests notice; passing `uniqueGuests` fixes this.

Only the client dialog checks that guest emails are unique; the server schema accepts duplicates. The handler only removes guests who are already attendees, so a request like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] creates two Attendee rows for the same email, because the Attendee table has no unique constraint. Enforce uniqueness on the server, for example by de-duplicating in the handler or adding a refine to the schema.

The handler filters the guests against an attendee list it read earlier, then calls createMany, with no transaction and no unique constraint on (bookingId, email). Two concurrent addGuests requests for the same booking can both pass the filter and insert the same guest twice. Re-check existing attendees inside a transaction, or add a unique constraint and use skipDuplicates.

sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. Guests that were filtered out because they were already attendees still receive the new-booking (AttendeeScheduledEmail) email instead of the guests-added email.

The variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner, but it is only true when the user passes both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner. A team admin who is not an owner therefore gets FORBIDDEN. Use || to match the intent.

The handler builds uniqueGuests by dropping existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original `guests`. Any existing attendee included in the input is treated as a new guest and gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass uniqueGuests.

blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased, but each guest is compared exactly as entered. A blacklisted address typed with any uppercase letters gets past the filter. Lowercase the guest email before comparing.

The booking is loaded with user.credentials, but EventManager is built from ctx.user and that user's own credentials. When an attendee or team admin adds guests, the update to the organizer's calendar event runs with the wrong user's credentials and will not find the event or will fail. Build EventManager from booking.user and its credentials.

The tooltip text "Remove email" is hard-coded in English. The rest of the component translates its text through t() from useLocale (for example t("add_another")), so users in other languages see this one string in English. Use a translation key instead.

The variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner, but the code joins the isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner checks with &&, so it is only true when both pass. Code that trusts the name will assume admins without the owner role are allowed. Use || so the logic matches the name.

The message is built with a template literal that always contains text, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the translated fallback. When err.data.code or err.message is missing, users see raw text like "undefined: " instead of the localized error.
The comment "These are like 40kb" appears to be copied from the phone input lazy loader. MultiEmail only uses existing UI components, so the size claim misleads readers about why it is lazy-loaded.

issues.descricao: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.
issues.textoGolden: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||. WHY: isTeamAdmin returns truthy for role ADMIN or OWNER while isTeamOwner returns true only for OWNER, so the && expression is only true for OWNERs; team ADMINs are treated as unauthorized and get FORBIDDEN when adding guests, contradicting the variable's intent. HOW: use `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`.

The flag is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&` (both admin AND owner). A team admin who is not the owner, or the owner who is not flagged admin, will fail this check, so the guard at line 54 wrongly throws FORBIDDEN for legitimate admins/owners. Use `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner.

The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` names an OR condition, but the code combines `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` with `&&`, so it is true only when the user is both admin AND owner. Either the name is wrong or the operator is; as written the permission check at line 54 denies a plain team admin, contradicting what the identifier promises. Use `||` to match the name (or rename if AND is intended).

issues.descricao: The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
issues.textoGolden: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The blacklist is compared case-sensitively against guest input while blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased. WHY: blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but the filter compares `guest` verbatim (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`); an authenticated user can add a blacklisted address simply by changing its case (e.g. `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`), bypassing the configured BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restriction. HOW: normalize the guest before comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.

Case-sensitivity bypass of the guest blacklist. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on the list side (line 71) but the input side is compared raw: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (line 77). A guest email submitted with any different casing (e.g. `Foo@Bar.com` when the blacklist holds `foo@bar.com`) passes the filter and is persisted, defeating BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Normalize the input before comparison, e.g. filter on `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (and likewise lowercase `guest` for the attendee dedup check).

WHAT: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming guest string is compared without lowercasing/normalizing. WHY: an attacker bypasses the blocklist with case variation (e.g. Spam@Example.com) and gets added/emailed.

issues.descricao: The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.
issues.textoGolden: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: uniqueGuests filter only dedupes against existing booking.attendees with case-sensitive === and never dedupes duplicates within the input guests array itself (server schema has no uniqueness refine unlike the client). WHY: a request with the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

uniqueGuests filters only against existing attendees/blacklist but never dedupes guests[] itself and schema has no uniqueness check. A request like guests=[a@x.com,a@x.com] passes the filter twice and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows or throws an unhandled DB unique-constraint exception. Dedupe/normalize input (and reject intra-request duplicates) before createMany.

uniqueGuests filters against existing attendees but does not deduplicate addresses within the incoming guests array. A direct mutation with the same new address twice inserts two Attendee records and sends duplicate invitations because the server schema permits duplicates and the Attendee model has no unique booking/email constraint. Deduplicate normalized input before filtering and inserting.

issues.descricao: Check-then-insert without a transaction or unique constraint lets two concurrent addGuests calls for the same email both pass the existing-attendee check and create duplicate attendees.

comentarios.texto: Race condition: findFirst check for existing attendees then booking.update+createMany is not atomic. Two concurrent addGuests calls with the same new email both see it as absent and both insert, creating duplicates. Guard with a unique constraint and handle conflict or run in a transaction/serializable check.

Check-then-insert race: the handler reads `booking.attendees` at the start, filters against it, then inserts in a separate `prisma.booking.update ... createMany` with no transaction or unique guard. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same guest both see it as absent and both insert, producing duplicate attendees. Wrap the read+filter+insert in a transaction (or rely on a unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and handle the conflict) so concurrent requests cannot both succeed.

issues.descricao: Attendee authorization and existing-attendee dedup compare emails case-sensitively, so an attendee with differently-cased stored email is FORBIDDEN and a case-variant of an existing attendee is added again.

comentarios.texto: Inconsistent email normalization for identity checks. Both the authorization check `attendee.email === user.email` (line 52) and the existing-attendee dedup `guest === attendee.email` (line 76) use strict case-sensitive equality, while emails are treated as case-insensitive everywhere else in this handler (the blacklist block directly below lowercases). Consequence: a legitimate attendee whose stored casing differs from their session email is wrongly FORBIDDEN, and a guest differing from an existing attendee only by case is duplicated rather than filtered. Compare on a normalized form (both sides `.toLowerCase()`), consistent with the blacklist normalization.

issues.descricao: The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.
issues.textoGolden: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests. WHY: already-existing attendees included in the request are misclassified as newGuests in email-manager and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (wrong notification).

Dead-transform / wrong input: `uniqueGuests` is computed (dedup vs existing attendees + blacklist) and written to DB, but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original `guests`. Existing attendees re-submitted are then `includes()`-matched as new and get AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

Pass `uniqueGuests` (the filtered set written to DB) to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of raw `guests`; the email layer assumes newGuests exactly equals newly created attendees for its Scheduled vs AddGuests branch.

issues.descricao: EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.

comentarios.texto: EventManager is initialized with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials. When an attendee or team owner adds guests to a booking whose calendar reference lacks credentialId, updateAllCalendarEvents selects credentials by type from the caller's calendars, so the organizer's event is not updated or the update targets the wrong account. Load credentials for booking.userId and initialize the manager with the booking owner.

issues.descricao: Claims a failing calendar update at addGuests.handler.ts:165 aborts the mutation after guests are persisted; the calendar update path already swallows provider errors.

comentarios.texto: The attendees are written to the database at line 92, but `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 runs outside the try/catch. If it throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests are already persisted, so the DB and the calendar are out of sync. No emails are sent, and a retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. Catch and handle the calendar update failure after the DB write.

The attendees are already committed to the DB when `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited without a try/catch. If the calendar sync throws, the mutation returns an error and skips the emails, although the guests were added. The caller sees a failure for a partly applied change and may retry. Handle calendar sync failure as best-effort, as the email send is, or run it before the DB write.

issues.descricao: Claims any attendee can add guests and trigger invites; this is the deliberate permission model of the new feature.

comentarios.texto: Any attendee, matched only by email, is allowed to add arbitrary guests to a booking, and the handler then sends emails and calendar invites on the organizer's behalf. Any attendee can use this to send invites to arbitrary addresses. Restrict the action to the organizer and team admins, or verify that the attendee's email is confirmed.

issues.descricao: The guests array has no server-side size limit, so any authorized caller, including an attendee, can add thousands of guests and trigger an unbounded batch of inserts and emails.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: guests is an unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length. WHY: any authorized caller (including a mere attendee) can submit thousands of emails causing unbounded createMany inserts plus unbounded Promise.all email fanout in sendAddGuestsEmails.

The mutation accepts an unbounded guest array that is persisted and immediately expanded into concurrent emails to every attendee. For non-seated bookings each email's ICS serializes the full attendee list, so adding N guests creates O(N) concurrent sends and O(N²) aggregate attachment work; repeated additions also resend to all existing attendees. Enforce a server-side guest-count and total-attendee limit before insertion and bound notification concurrency.

issues.descricao: The Remove email tooltip in MultiEmail is a hard-coded English string instead of a translation key.

comentarios.texto: Tooltip content="Remove email" is hard-coded English user-facing text bypassing i18n while surrounding strings in the same file/PR use t(). Wrap it in t() e.g. content={t("remove_email")} and add the key to locales.

`Tooltip content="Remove email"` is a hard-coded English user-facing string, while the surrounding code in this same component routes user text through `t()` (e.g. `t("add_another")` on line 69). This string bypasses the translation mechanism and will never be localised; it should use a translation key.

The new removal tooltip hard-codes `Remove email`, so users in non-English locales see English text even though the neighbouring controls use `t(...)` and this component already obtains `t` from useLocale. Route this tooltip through a translation key (and supply its English translation) rather than using the literal.

issues.descricao: The onError fallback to unable_to_add_guests is unreachable because the template-string message is always truthy.

comentarios.texto: Unreachable fallback: `message` is a template string `${code}: ${...}` which is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never takes the fallback. Build message conditionally or test the underlying parts for emptiness.

In `onError`, `message` is always a non-empty template string (`"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"`), so the fallback `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable and the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` translation is never shown. The user is instead shown a raw error code prefix like `BAD_REQUEST: ...` rather than the translated message; the fallback and code prefix handling should be corrected so the intended translated text reaches the user.

The error message is built as a template string, so it is always truthy. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is therefore dead code, and the user can see "undefined: ..." or an untranslated raw message. Use `err.message ? t(err.message) : t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

issues.descricao: After a validation failure followed by a successful add, isInvalidEmail stays true, so the stale emails_must_be_unique_valid error shows the next time the dialog is opened.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: addGuestsMutation onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never resets isInvalidEmail. WHY: after one failed validation the red emails_must_be_unique_valid error persists on the next open/successful add.

issues.descricao: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.
issues.textoGolden: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

issues.descricao: The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
The addGuests FORBIDDEN error uses the translation key you_do_not_have_permission, which is missing from the locale files, so the dialog shows the raw key to users.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParse result object, and that object is written directly as credential.key. WHY: the DB key becomes {success, data}, so googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) at line 75 throws for every later request and the Google credential becomes unusable after the first refresh. HOW: store the parsed data.

WHAT: when credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data as if it were a Gaxios response. WHY: token is undefined, so token.access_token throws a TypeError and Google tokens can never be refreshed in sync mode. HOW: in the sync branch, parse the Response JSON before using it, or make refreshOAuthTokens return the same shape that each caller expects.

WHAT: credentialId is passed where refreshOAuthTokens expects the credential's userId. WHY: the sync endpoint receives a credential id as calcomUserId, so it returns tokens for the wrong user or for none. HOW: pass the credential's userId instead.

WHAT: in sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this code reads tokenInfo.data.error as if it were an axios response. WHY: tokenInfo.data is undefined, so the property access throws and the token refresh always fails when sync is enabled. HOW: await the Response's json() in the sync branch and use that value as the token data.

WHAT: both computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal property name '[object Object]', so the schema only declares access_token plus a field named '[object Object]'. WHY: zod strips every other field (expires_in, expiry_date, scope, token_type), so sync-mode refreshes lose expiry information and callers such as Zoom (expires_in) and office365 get NaN or missing values. HOW: use z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough(), with explicit optional expiry fields if needed.

WHAT: when the parsed response has no refresh_token, the code writes the literal string "refresh_token" into it. WHY: office365calendar spreads tokenResponse.data over the stored credentials (line 264), so a provider response without refresh_token (always the case with the stripping minimum schema) replaces the real stored refresh token with the string 'refresh_token', and the next refresh fails. HOW: remove the placeholder assignment so callers keep their existing refresh_token.

WHAT: the new code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file never imports prisma. Imports at lines 1-20 have no @calcom/prisma. WHY: this causes a TypeScript compile error or a ReferenceError at runtime, which rejects getClient so every Salesforce operation fails. HOW: add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

WHAT: success is detected by comparing response.statusText to "OK". WHY: statusText is empty over HTTP/2 and in many fetch implementations, so successful refreshes throw a 400 and the Salesforce client can never be created. HOW: check response.ok instead.

WHAT: the token is refreshed and saved, but jsforce.Connection is still built with the old credentialKey.access_token and instance_url. WHY: the refresh result is discarded for the current connection, so requests use the stale or expired token. HOW: pass accessTokenParsed.data.access_token and accessTokenParsed.data.instance_url to the Connection.

WHAT: getClient runs on every SalesforceCalendarService construction and always makes a token refresh HTTP call plus a credential DB write, without checking whether the token is expired. WHY: this adds an external round-trip and a DB write to every booking or calendar operation, and frequent refreshes can hit Salesforce rate limits. HOW: refresh only when the token is invalid or expired, or rely on jsforce's built-in refresh handling.

WHAT: appStoreMetadata is indexed by app.slug, but the map is keyed by app directory name (see _appRegistry.ts:17, which uses app.dirName). WHY: for apps whose slug differs from their dirName (e.g. google-calendar vs googlecalendar), the lookup returns undefined and the webhook always responds 404, so those credentials cannot be synced. HOW: select dirName from prisma.app and index appStoreMetadata by it.

WHAT: the webhook secret is checked with a plain !== string comparison. WHY: this endpoint can overwrite any user's third-party credentials, and a non-constant-time comparison exposes the secret to timing analysis. HOW: compare using crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers after confirming the header is a string.

WHAT: when state.teamId is present, the code only checks that the user is an accepted team member before creating a team credential, and throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam runs only on the path where teamId is falsy, so it is effectively a no-op. WHY: any non-admin team member can install OAuth apps on behalf of the team through a crafted state parameter. HOW: call throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state.teamId, userId }) inside the teamId branch before prisma.credential.create.

WHAT: in sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the result is used directly as a HubspotToken. WHY: expiresIn and accessToken are undefined on a Response, so expiryDate becomes NaN, a Response object is persisted as the credential key, and setAccessToken(undefined) is called. HOW: parse the Response JSON in the sync branch before treating it as a token.

The webhook secret is checked with `!==`, which can leak timing information and let an attacker recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET byte by byte. Anyone with the secret can overwrite any user's app credentials. Compare in constant time with crypto.timingSafeEqual, after confirming the header is a string and the lengths match.

`refreshOAuthTokens` gets `credentialId` (the Credential row id) as its `userId` argument. With credential sync enabled, it asks the sync endpoint for the tokens of the user whose id equals that credential id and saves them onto this credential. As a result, one user's Zoho Bigin access token is stored under another user's account and can be used by them; pass the credential owner's userId instead.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturn ({success, data}), but this code saves that whole object as credential.key. The stored Google credential then holds {success, data} instead of access_token/refresh_token/expiry_date, which breaks later reads. Persist `.data` instead.

refreshOAuthTokens declares its third parameter as userId and sends it to the sync endpoint as calcomUserId. This call passes credentialId instead, so in sync mode the endpoint is asked for tokens for the wrong (or a nonexistent) user. Pass the credential's userId instead.

When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this code reads `res?.data` as if it were a googleapis response. That makes `token` undefined, so reading `token.access_token` throws and the refresh fails every time in sync mode. Parse the body with `await res.json()` when the sync path is used.

The comments say any numeric property is treated as the expiry and that other properties are allowed. In fact `z.string().toString()` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]", so both lines define that one key and the second overrides the first. Neither documented behaviour exists, so the schema validates a meaningless key instead of an expiry field and does not explicitly pass through extra fields.

refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`, but here it receives the credential id. The sync endpoint is therefore told a credential id is a Cal.com user id, which looks up the wrong user (or none) and also bypasses the user-ownership check. Pass the credential's userId instead, for example by giving it to refreshAccessToken.

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `safeParse` (`{success, data}`), not the parsed credentials. Before this change, `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the plain credential object. Now `prisma.credential.update` stores `{success: true, data: {...}}` as the key, so the next read of `access_token` or `refresh_token` from the key finds nothing and authentication breaks.

`refreshOAuthTokens` sends its third argument to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`. When credential sync is enabled, the endpoint gets tokens for an unrelated user, or for no user, and those tokens are used for this credential.

When sync is enabled, this returns a fetch `Response`. The HubSpot, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin callers expect a parsed token object or an axios response and read fields like `.data.error`. On a `Response`, `.data` is undefined, so `.data.error` throws a TypeError and the token refresh fails every time sync is on.

`googleCredentialSchema.parse()` used to return the key object, but `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result (`{ success, data }`). That whole wrapper now gets saved as `credential.key`. On the next read, `googleCredentialSchema` and `getGoogleAuth` won't find `access_token` or `refresh_token` at the top level, so every Google credential breaks after its first refresh. Store `.data` instead.

The third parameter of `refreshOAuthTokens` is the Cal.com `userId`, which the sync endpoint receives as `calcomUserId`. This consumer passes `credentialId`, so the parent app is asked for tokens belonging to the wrong user, or to a user that doesn't exist. Pass the credential's `userId` (it needs to be threaded through from `credential.userId`).

When credential sync is enabled, this function returns a fetch `Response`. The google, zoho-bigin and zohocrm callers still read `res.data` / `tokenInfo.data`, which is undefined on a `Response`, so the token refresh throws a TypeError whenever sync is on. Either have the sync path return the shape each caller expects, or update those callers to call `await response.json()`.
The zoho-bigin change passes `credentialId` where a user id is expected. The reviewer flagged this as outside the assigned scope.
The Google Calendar change stores the whole `safeParse` result object as the credential key instead of only the parsed data. The reviewer flagged this as outside the assigned scope.
The computed keys in the zod schema (`[z.string().toString()]`) do not do what the comments describe. The reviewer flagged this as outside the assigned scope.
In `createOAuthAppCredential`, the team branch checks only team membership and not admin access. The reviewer flagged this as outside the assigned scope.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturn object (`{success, data}`), not the parsed credentials. That whole wrapper is written to `credential.key`, so the stored key no longer has access_token/refresh_token at the top level. Later reads of the credential then fail. Store `.data` instead.

refreshOAuthTokens takes a userId as its third argument and sends it to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Here it gets `credentialId` (credential.id), so the external app is asked for tokens for the wrong user. The guard also fires for team credentials, which other callers exclude by passing userId=null.

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both become the same literal key, "[object Object]", so the second overwrites the first and the number/expiry rule is never applied. Because z.object strips unknown keys, the parsed data drops expiry and every other field except access_token. In sync mode this loses the expiry date. Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` instead.

When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response instead of the gaxios result. That Response has no `.data` property, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. Because of this, Google token refresh always fails in sync mode. Parse the Response body as JSON in that branch.

issues.descricao: The new app-credential webhook checks its shared secret with a plain !== string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information about the secret.

comentarios.texto: Direct !== comparison of webhook secret leaks via timing attack. Use constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on hashed/buffered values with length check) instead of `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

The webhook authenticates a secret using direct string inequality, which is not constant-time and can leak information about the secret through comparison timing. Compare fixed-length representations using a constant-time primitive (such as crypto.timingSafeEqual), handling absent or malformed headers safely, instead of comparing the secret strings directly.

The webhook secret is compared with the `!==` operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the secret via response timing (timing attack). An attacker can iteratively recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and then forge requests that create/update arbitrary user credential keys (decrypted with the AES key) via this endpoint. Use a constant-time comparison, e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, guarding for length mismatch first.

issues.descricao: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
issues.textoGolden: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: zod parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse throw unhandled (no try/catch) with no method guard. WHY: Invalid body/keys or GET request crashes handler with 500 and leaks stack, instead of 400/405. HOW: Wrap parse/decrypt in try/catch returning 400 and restrict to POST.

schema .parse plus symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse throw unhandled (ZodError, decrypt error, SyntaxError) on invalid body or tampered keys, crashing webhook with 500. Use safeParse and try/catch with 400 responses.

issues.descricao: The webhook's non-atomic findFirst-then-create lets concurrent deliveries for the same user and app insert duplicate credential rows.

comentarios.texto: The webhook performs a non-atomic findFirst followed by create when no credential exists. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and insert duplicates because Credential has no unique userId/appId constraint; subsequent findFirst updates only one duplicate, leaving competing credentials stale. Serialize the lookup/create operation for each user/app pair or introduce an appropriate uniqueness constraint and atomic upsert.

issues.descricao: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.
issues.textoGolden: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: The parser fabricates the literal refresh token "refresh_token" whenever a successful response omits refresh_token, including when synchronization is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits that omission, and its caller merges parsed data over existing credentials, replacing the valid saved refresh token with this invalid value and breaking the next refresh. Leave the property absent so the existing token survives the merge.

When a refresh response omits refresh_token, this helper manufactures the hardcoded credential "refresh_token". Callers such as Office365 merge this into stored credentials, overwriting the valid existing refresh token and causing subsequent provider refreshes to use a predictable invalid token. Leave the field absent and preserve the existing credential when omission is allowed by the provider, or reject the response when a refresh token is required; do not substitute a literal authentication token.

WHAT: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal string "refresh_token". WHY: Stores bogus refresh token in DB, breaking all future refreshes and masking provider errors. HOW: Preserve existing credential refresh_token or throw instead of injecting placeholder.

issues.descricao: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
issues.textoGolden: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

comentarios.texto: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a fixed string key such as "ZodString", so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires a literal numeric property with that name. Every synced token response fails validation and throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", not a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property named "[object Object]", so safeParse always fails in credential-sync mode and the function throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` on an object with access_token and optional numeric expiry fields instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a literal string like "ZodString" and not to a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that nonsense name and never matches real token responses. In sync mode every refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` and a real expiry check instead.

issues.descricao: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect their provider-specific shapes (res.data, axios .data, HubspotToken), so token refresh breaks for Google, Zoho and HubSpot when credential sharing is on.
issues.textoGolden: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: In the credential-sharing branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object instead of a parsed token payload, yet several callers treat the result as an already-parsed token object.
WHY: Callers such as hubspot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`), zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`), zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and googlecalendar (`res?.data`) read `.data`/token fields off the return value; a `Response` has neither, so the sync path yields `undefined`/`NaN` or throws a TypeError — the feature's primary code path is broken for those apps.
HOW: Parse the response (e.g. `const data = await response.json(); return data;`) before returning, or make every caller await the appropriate response handler.

In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response (no `.data`), but the google caller reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, throwing a TypeError swallowed by the catch, so the token is never refreshed.

`res?.data` assumes the value returned by refreshOAuthTokens has a `.data` field (true for the `fetchTokens.res` branch), but when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the helper returns a raw `fetch()` Response, which has no `.data`. Then `token.access_token` throws. Either parse the shared-mode Response here or have refreshOAuthTokens return a normalized `{ data }` shape.

issues.descricao: Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
issues.textoGolden: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result {success,data}, not the parsed key. Storing it directly as `key` writes the wrapper to the credential. Unwrap like other callers: check .success and use .data.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse result {success,data}, but call site stores that wrapper as credential `key` (previously googleCredentialSchema.parse() returned the plain object). Store `key.data` / handle wrapper, otherwise persisted credential becomes {success,data} shape and subsequent credential reads fail.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse wrapper {success,data} but code stores the whole wrapper as credential.key. Office365calendar in same PR unwraps via .data. Persisted credential will be {success,data} instead of tokens, so next load fails validation. Unwrap to .data after success check.

issues.descricao: After switching to parseRefreshTokenResponse, the tokenResponse.success check in Office365 refreshAccessToken is dead code and the previous error logging was dropped.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws when parsing fails, so the `tokenResponse.success` check on the next line is dead code and the previous error logging was removed. A failed refresh now throws out of refreshAccessToken instead of keeping the old credentials. Catch the error or restore the previous handling.

issues.descricao: Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.

comentarios.texto: getClient now unconditionally exchanges the Salesforce refresh token on every service construction, even when the saved access token is valid. Each constructor invocation adds a blocking OAuth network round trip and credential database write before any Salesforce operation, replacing jsforce's existing on-demand refresh behavior. Keep refresh on demand or guard the exchange with a token-expiration check.

issues.descricao: The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.

comentarios.texto: The new credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it; searching this file finds only the new usage. This fails TypeScript checking and raises ReferenceError after a successful token exchange at runtime. Import prisma from @calcom/prisma before using it.

issues.descricao: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id instead of the user id to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong calcomUserId.
issues.textoGolden: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The 3rd argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (= `credential.id`, line 53), but the function's parameter is `userId` (`refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)`).
WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the sync endpoint is sent `calcomUserId: <credential id>` instead of the user id, so Bigin credentials are synced against the wrong/non-existent user (all other apps correctly pass `credential.userId`).
HOW: Pass `credential.userId` instead of `credentialId` as the third argument.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the Cal.com userId (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync request and to decide whether sharing runs), but this call passes `credentialId`. Every other caller passes `credential.userId`, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential row id as the user id and shared credentials are fetched/updated for the wrong identity. Pass `credential.userId` here.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId` (declared in refreshOAuthTokens.ts line 3 and used as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`), but this call passes `credentialId` (the Credential row id, line 53) instead of the user id. When credential sharing is enabled the customer's sync endpoint receives a credential id labelled as calcomUserId and cannot resolve the correct Cal.com user. Pass `credential.userId` (the BiginToken/credential payload carries it) or plumb the user id through refreshAccessToken.

issues.descricao: Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
issues.textoGolden: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Checks response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok and builds jsforce.Connection from stale credentialKey.access_token/instance_url ignoring accessTokenParsed.data. WHY: Refresh never takes effect (old token reused) and valid refreshes can throw on runtimes where statusText is empty. HOW: Check !response.ok and use parsed access_token/instance_url for connection and DB update.

issues.descricao: After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.
issues.textoGolden: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The new block fetches and persists a fresh access token (`accessTokenParsed.data`) but then creates the `jsforce.Connection` with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106) instead of the just-refreshed token.
WHY: The refreshed token is written to the DB but never used for the connection; if the old token was expired, jsforce must refresh again (extra round trip) or fail, and the DB/connection state diverge.
HOW: Pass the new access token (`accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`) to the `jsforce.Connection`.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The `retryCount > 1` branch of the deleteMany OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so the SMS cron deletes any WorkflowReminder (email or WhatsApp) whose retryCount is above 1. WHY: Once another cron starts incrementing retryCount, this job will silently delete reminders for other methods. HOW: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount condition.

WHAT: The new retryCount increment sits inside `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)`, so a reminder with a missing phone number or an empty message never increments its counter. WHY: These reminders can never succeed, but they are still re-fetched and re-processed on every cron run until scheduledDate passes, which is the behavior the PR is meant to stop. HOW: Move the increment into an else branch of the outer `if` as well, or into one failure path that covers both cases.

WHAT: The prisma.workflowReminder.update added in the catch block has no guard, so if it throws (for example P2025 because the reminder was deleted, or a DB error), the exception escapes the for-loop. WHY: All remaining reminders in this cron run are skipped and the handler returns an error instead of continuing. HOW: Wrap the catch-block update in its own try/catch, or use updateMany, which does not throw when no row matches.

WHAT: Every failure from twilio.scheduleSMS increments retryCount, including temporary ones: an undefined return while the account is SMS-locked, a throw from checkSMSRateLimit when the monthly limit is hit, and Twilio network or 5xx errors. WHY: Two consecutive cron runs with a temporary failure permanently delete a valid reminder, so the attendee never gets the SMS even after the condition clears. HOW: Increment retryCount only for permanent errors, such as Twilio invalid-number error codes, and let temporary errors retry without counting.

WHAT: retryCount is written as `reminder.retryCount + 1` from a value read earlier, not with an atomic increment. WHY: Overlapping cron invocations processing the same reminder overwrite each other and lose increments. HOW: Use `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`.

The comment says only past-dated SMS reminders are deleted, but the new OR branch also deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, whatever its method or scheduled date. Update the comment so it describes both deletion criteria and readers aren't misled about which reminders are removed.

The `retryCount > 1` branch of the OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so this SMS cron will delete any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, ...) whose retryCount exceeds 1. The comment and the rest of the handler are scoped to SMS, but this clause isn't. Add the method filter inside this branch so the cleanup only touches SMS reminders.

Before this change, the per-reminder catch block only logged, so one bad reminder never stopped the cron run. It now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` without a guard, so if that update throws (DB error, or the record was deleted at the same time), the exception escapes the loop. The handler then fails and all remaining reminders in this run go unscheduled.

The new update in the catch block can throw. That happens if the reminder was deleted concurrently (for example, its booking was cancelled), which gives P2025, or if the original error was a DB failure. The throw escapes the for loop, so every remaining reminder is skipped and the handler returns a 500 instead of carrying on. Use updateMany, which does not throw when no row matches, and catch any error from it so one failed reminder cannot stop the batch.

The second OR branch deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, whatever its method. This SMS cron can therefore delete EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders as soon as any other path starts using retryCount. Add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to this branch.

The retryCount branch of the OR condition in the cleanup is not limited to SMS reminders, so it may delete or affect non-SMS reminders. The reviewer flagged this as outside their assigned review class.
The retry counter is updated with a read-then-write instead of an atomic increment. Concurrent runs could lose updates. The reviewer flagged this as outside their assigned review class.

issues.descricao: retryCount is set to reminder.retryCount + 1 from a value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment, so overlapping runs can lose increments.
issues.textoGolden: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: retryCount is incremented with a read-value computed at the start of the run (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) instead of an atomic increment. WHY: if two cron invocations overlap (or the same reminder is processed twice before the write commits), both read the same retryCount and both write N+1, so failures are undercounted and the reminder can loop forever without ever reaching the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold. HOW: use `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` so the increment is atomic (the initial read value is then irrelevant).

`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` is a read-modify-write of the value fetched at the top of the handler, not an atomic increment. Two overlapping cron runs both read the same retryCount and both write the same +1, losing an update, so failed reminders can be retried indefinitely and never reach the `gt: 1` deletion threshold. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead of computing from the stale in-memory value (same issue in the else branch at lines 179-186).

Retry counts are assigned from the stale findMany snapshot instead of incremented atomically, both here and in the catch branch. Two overlapping cron requests can each fail scheduling the same reminder with retryCount zero and both write one, so two failed attempts do not reach the deletion threshold and additional attempts are scheduled. Use Prisma's atomic retryCount increment operation in both failure branches.

issues.descricao: The deleteMany OR clause applies retryCount > 1 without the SMS method filter, so the SMS cron deletes any workflow reminder (email, WhatsApp) with retryCount above 1.
issues.textoGolden: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

comentarios.texto: The comment "//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date" no longer describes the deleteMany below it.
